you're travelling on an emergency passport
the name and/or photo in your passport are different from how you present
Lost or stolen passport
Your passport is valuable and can be used by others to commit crimes.
Don’t let anyone trick you into giving it to them. Always keep it in a safe place.

In Australia: contact the Australian Passport Information Service.
Overseas: contact the nearest Australian embassy or consulate.
Passport with ‘X’ gender identifier

Ask the embassy or consulate of your destinations if they’ll accept your passport with an 'X' gender marker. Check all transit destinations too.

Visas
You need a visa to visit Uganda.

The East African Community's EAC Tourist Visa allows travellers multiple entries to Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda for 90 days. Another option is to apply for a visa from the Government of Uganda. Apply for the EAC Tourist Visa or a Ugandan visa by using Uganda's online visa application.
Border measures

If you're travelling from Uganda, you may be subject to entry restrictions, health screening or quarantine in other countries. Contact your airline directly for the latest updates and check the entry requirements of the destinations you're travelling to or transiting.
Ensure you review and comply with testing and health screening requirements for any transit and destination countries. Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice.
The border with DRC remains closed.
Yellow fever vaccination
You don't need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Uganda, but some airlines may require one when you leave and you will need to show it when you return to Australia.
Vaccination is recommended for protection against yellow fever for travellers over 9 months of age. Some exemptions may apply. Talk to your doctor about vaccinations before you travel.
Find out about returning to Australia after exposure to yellow fever.

Australians holding ordinary passports who wish to visit Türkiye don't need a visa for tourism, business or transit purposes if staying for 90 days or less in a 180-day period. If you intend to stay longer, you must apply for a Turkish residence permit.
Different entry rules may apply when travelling with a temporary passport or an emergency travel document.

If you're not travelling for tourism, business, medical treatment, or transit for under 90 days, you may need to arrange a visa through an embassy or consulate of Türkiye before you arrive. If you don't, authorities may refuse you entry.
If you're a tourist and arrive by sea, make sure you get entry and exit stamps in your passport.
If you don't abide by the terms of your visa or permit, you may be fined, deported, and banned from re-entering Türkiye.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest embassy or consulate for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.

prima: Each country or territory decides its own entry and exit rules, including health border screening measures. To find out what you need to enter a destination, ask their embassy, consulate or immigration office.
Visas

If you're visiting Thailand for tourism or short-term travel, you may be able to get a visa exemption (visa-free travel). You may only be allowed to enter Thailand on 2 visa-free entries each calendar year if you don't have a justifiable reason.

Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months before entering. Be ready to show proof of your accommodation in Thailand, enough funds for your stay and your onward or return flight ticket. You may be refused entry if you can't show these documents.

You must complete a Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) within 3 days before arriving in Thailand. The TDAC is free of charge and must be submitted online through the Thailand Immigration Bureau website. Beware of fake websites charging you a fee for the TDAC.

If you require an E-Visa, you can apply through the Official Thai E-Visa website. You can only apply if you're currently not in Thailand and in a country where E-visa services are available. You're no longer required to submit your passports and supporting documents in person at the Royal Thai Embassy/Consulate-General. After your E-Visa application has been approved, you'll receive a confirmation email, which you can print and show to airlines and Thai immigration officials when entering Thailand.
You must get an entry stamp from an immigration officer at the point of entry into Thailand. Don't get your visa, visa extension or entry stamp from visa shops or travel agents in Thailand.
A passport that has been altered or that contains counterfeit visas and entry/exit stamps is deemed invalid. You may be arrested, prosecuted and/or deported.

Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest Embassy or consulate of Thailand, the Royal Thai Embassy Canberra or Royal Thai Consulate-General Sydney. See the official website of the Tourism Authority of Thailand for the latest details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.

Before entering Thailand, understand your visa conditions, entry and exit requirements, including if you travel by private sea vessel. The Australian Government can't intervene in immigration, customs or quarantine matters in other countries. Thailand immigration and visa decisions are final. The Australian Government can't help you.
Visa overstays
If you overstay your visa, you'll need to pay a fine before you can leave. You can also be:
arrested
prosecuted
jailed
deported
banned from re-entering Thailand.
Thai authorities can blacklist you, which means you can never return to Thailand.
Penalties for not paying the fine include long prison sentences. Conditions at Immigration Detention Centres are harsh.
More information:
Thai Immigration Bureau
Border measures
You may be subject to biometric screening at points of entry. Clarify entry requirements with your airline, International Air Transport Association (IATA) or your nearest Thai Embassy.

If you’ve stayed in or transited through Ebola disease-affected countries, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, you’ll be subject to health screening and may be required to quarantine or self-isolate for at least 21 days. For more information, contact Thailand’s Department of Disease Control hotline on 1422.

If you're travelling from a Yellow Fever-endemic country or a country with Mpox outbreaks, pre-register through the Thai Health Pass digital platform before checking in with the airline at the country of origin.
Travel within Thailand
Foreign passengers must present their passport for domestic flights within Thailand. You may be refused boarding if you're unable to present your passport or if it's damaged.
Departure from Thailand
Speak with your airline or travel provider for information about departing Thailand.
More information:
Royal Thai Embassy, Canberra
IATA

prima: Each country or territory decides its own entry and exit rules, including health border screening measures. To find out what you need to enter a destination, ask their embassy, consulate or immigration office.
Visas
You need a visa to enter Tanzania. Apply for an eVisa online before travelling.

It's possible to get some single-entry visas on arrival in Tanzania at the main points of entry, if you meet all the requirements for entry. You may also be required to provide proof of your return journey.

You must purchase inbound travel insurance from the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) prior to arrival in mainland Tanzania. For travel to Zanzibar, you must purchase insurance from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC). There are limits to what is covered by this insurance. Make sure you also have separate comprehensive travel insurance.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact an embassy or consulate of Tanzania for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules and the online visa application form.
More information:
Tanzanian Immigration
Visit Zanzibar
Border measures

Immigration authorities at the port of entry determine who can enter the country. If you intend to travel to Tanzania, confirm entry requirements with Tanzanian authorities prior to making any travel arrangements. Refer to the latest requirements on the Ministry of Health’s website.
Ebola disease
You must undertake Ebola disease health screening and body temperature checks on arrival in Tanzania.
If you’re coming from the DRC or Uganda, you also need to complete a Traveller’s Surveillance Form before departure or on arrival.

Health screening on arrival and entry restrictions for travellers who have visited countries affected by Ebola may be imposed with limited notice and can change quickly, including for transit passengers. Check the latest requirements with your airline or travel provider before departure.
More information:
Tanzania Ministry of Health Traveller’s Health Surveillance
Yellow fever vaccination
You'll need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Tanzania if arriving from a yellow fever risk country. Some airlines may want to see one when you leave.
Find out about returning to Australia after exposure to yellow fever.
More information:
Countries with a risk of yellow fever
Mpox
You'll need to pass through Mpox screening, including body temperature checks, at all points of entry into Tanzania.

Visas

In most circumstances, such as tourism, travel for business meetings or conferences, Australian passport holders do not require a visa for stays up to 90 days. Other passport holders should check with the Singapore Immigration and Checkpoint Authority if they need a visa to enter Singapore. ICA | Check if You Need an Entry Visa
At immigration, you may have to show:
a passport with at least 6 months validity
evidence of enough funds for your intended stay
a confirmed onward or return flight ticket
a valid visa to enter your next destination
yellow fever vaccination certificate, if required ICA | Yellow Fever Vaccination Certificate
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest high commission, embassy or consulate of Singapore for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.
If you breach your visa conditions or overstay your visa, authorities may fine, detain, cane and/or deport you.
Employment Visa
You'll need to apply for a visa to be employed or study in Singapore. Check work visa information with the Ministry of Manpower.
Border measures
On arrival, you'll need to show:

your completed Singapore Arrival Card (SGAC) (there is no charge for the SGAC). This can be completed within three days of your arrival. There are scam websites that ask for payment. Make sure you use the official ICA website.
a yellow fever vaccination certificate, if needed
More information is available on the ICA | Entering, Transiting and Departing website.
Be careful of scam websites imitating official Singapore Arrival Card website.
Transit through Singapore
See Changi Airport website for more information on transiting.
Do not bring medicinal cannabis to Singapore, even during transit. If you take prescribed medicinal cannabis, you should contact the Singapore Health Science Authority to review your situation.
Check flight schedules directly with your airline. Confirm your arrangements with your airline or travel agent before travelling.

Expect to be screened during your transit. You may be security screened when boarding your flight to Singapore and before boarding your connecting flight. See Changi Airport website for further information on transit requirements.
Check the Immigration & Checkpoints Authority website or Changi Airport for the latest advice.
Misuse of boarding pass
It's illegal to enter the transit area of Singapore’s Changi Airport for any purpose other than departing Singapore on a flight.

entering the transit area with a valid boarding pass but without planning to travel, such as for shopping, meeting people or seeing off loved ones, is an offence. Individuals who do so may be arrested upon re-entry into Singapore.
offenders may be fined up to SGD 20,000 and/or jailed for up to two years.

Australia and other countries have placed sanctions on Russia. Russia's response to these sanctions may disrupt travel.
Visas
You need a visa to enter Russia unless you're travelling on certain commercial cruise ships.
You can't get a visa on arrival.
If you arrive without a valid visa, authorities will fine, detain and deport you at your own expense. They may bar you from re-entering.
Make sure you apply for the correct visa type, such as a 'tourist' or 'visitor' visa.
If your visa type doesn't match the purpose of your visit, authorities may:
not let you enter
detain you
You may need to provide biometric fingerprints for the visa application process.
After you get your Russian visa, check your visa details are correct, including the following:
full name
passport number
date of birth
visa type
intention of stay
validity dates
If there are errors, return your passport to the Russian Embassy or Consulate for visa detail correction.
It's impossible to amend visa details once you're in Russia.
Border measures
If, despite our advice, you decide to enter Russia, expect thorough security checks at the border, including questioning, fingerprints/DNA sampling and inspections of electronic devices.
You're required to submit your biometric personal data on arrival, including being photographed and fingerprint scanning.

Biometric data will be collected at all border checkpoints, including Moscow international airports Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky. Children under 6, diplomats, employees of international organisations accredited in Russia, and their family members are exempt from this requirement.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest embassy or consulate for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.
More information:
Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Road Travel

There are currently severe fuel shortages throughout Russia. Most regions report disruptions in supplies and have introduced fuel rationing. In some regions, bus services have been cut, fares raised, and garbage collection halted.
Russia has temporarily relaxed fuel requirements, allowing production and circulation of Euro 3 fuel up until 31 December 2026.
If you intend to drive in Russia, you should understand your vehicle's limitations and check fuel quality and availability before travelling.
More information:
Russia's official legislation publications (in Russian)

You'll need a valid visa or Nigerian residence permit to travel to or reside in Nigeria. You can check visa conditions and apply and pay for a visa online through the Nigeria Immigration Service website. To complete the process, you may need to provide your passport by mail or in person to the appropriate Nigerian diplomatic mission in your country.
Significant penalties, including fines and detention, may apply for people who overstay their visa terms.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest embassy, high commission or consulate of Nigeria for details about visas, customs and quarantine rules.
Border measures

Expect enhanced security and health screening measures at airports. Foreign nationals must complete landing and departure cards before arriving and departing. You may be asked to show these at airports, including prior to boarding your flight.

Nigerian authorities have introduced enhanced public health measures at international entry points in response to the current Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.

You're required to complete an online Health Declaration Form from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) portal before boarding your flight. If you're unable to complete the form in advance of travel, you'll need to complete the form on arrival.
You may also be subject to additional health screening measures on arrival, such as travel history and body temperature checks.
More information:
Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention

Check you meet all entry and insurance requirements before you travel.

Italy is part of the Schengen area, along with many other European countries, which means you can enter Italy without a visa in some cases.
If, for unexpected reasons, you can't return to Australia or leave Italy before your visa-free limit expires, contact the nearest local immigration office ('questura') in Italy.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest Italian embassy or consulate for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.

If you believe your entry, exit, or length of stay in the Schengen area has been recorded incorrectly in the Entry/Exit System (EES), you should raise the issue with border authorities the next time you cross an external Schengen border and request that the record be corrected. You may be required to provide supporting documentation.
Travellers who are exempt from EES requirements should carry documentation confirming their exemption status when travelling.
For further information on data protection rights and procedures for correcting inaccurate or incomplete records visit Entry-Exit System (EES) | Polizia di Stato.
Border with Slovenia

Temporary border checks have been introduced at Italy's borders with Slovenia. Allow extra time when crossing the land border between Italy and Slovenia and be ready to show your passport or residency card if you're asked to do so by the border police. Checks may also involve vehicle inspections.
Travel from Spain
Temporary border checks are in place for arrivals from Spain at airports and seaports. Be ready to show your passport or residency card if you're asked by border police. Allow extra time for travel.

prima: Each country or territory decides its own entry and exit rules, including health border screening measures. To find out what you need to enter a destination, ask their embassy, consulate or immigration office.
Visa requirements

You must apply for a visa before arrival. Check if you're eligible for an e-visa on the Indian Visa Online website. For information on other visa categories or entry and exit requirements, see the Indian High Commission in Australia website.
For information and advice on Indian visas and immigration regulations while in India, see the FRRO/FRO and the Bureau of Immigration websites.

If your visa has expired or you have overstayed your visa, speak to the Foreigners Registration Office (FRRO/FRO) before you attempt to travel. Immigration authorities may prevent you from leaving India on an expired visa.

If your baby was born in India, you must let the FRRO know of the birth and that you'll apply for Australian citizenship and a passport for your child. Make sure you obtain an Australian citizenship certificate and an Australian passport, as well as an Indian visa to remain legally in India or to travel. If you don't inform the FRRO, you'll have to pay a significant fine.
Electronic visas
You may be eligible for an Electronic Visa (e-Visa) for:
tourism
business
medical reasons
Get your e-Visa before travelling. You won't be able to get a visa on arrival.
Check that you're eligible before you apply. See the Government of India's Indian Visa Online website for details.
If you present an e-Visa at an entry point where the e-Visa is not recognised, you:
won't be able to apply for any other visa
won't be allowed to enter India
will be deported
Tourist e-Visa

Indian Tourist e-Visas can be granted for 30 days, one year or five years. There may be additional visa conditions on the maximum length of stay depending on your nationality. Detailed information regarding visa validity and the maximum length of stay for each visa category can be found on the Indian Visa Online and Ministry of Home Affairs websites.
Beware of fake websites offering e-Visa services.
Carry a printed copy of your e-Visa, known as an electronic travel authorisation (ETA).
You'll get a formal visa in your passport when you arrive.
Long queues are common at immigration counters, regardless of your visa type.
Not all international airports in India allow passengers to enter with an e-Visa. Check with your nearest Indian consulate, embassy or agent and organise a visa before you arrive.
If you have an e-Visa, you can leave India from any authorised immigration checkpoint.
Other visas
Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Card holders
Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cards are multiple entry, multi-purpose lifelong visas to visit India. OCI holders are entitled to live and work in India.

If you receive a new Australian passport and hold an OCI card, you must update your details on the OCI portal. You must do this every time you renew your Australian passport or receive a new Australian passport.
More information:
Overseas Citizen of India Services
e-Arrival Card
You're required to complete the online e-Arrival Card up to 3 days before travel to India. This applies to Australian citizens and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card holders.
Depending on your travel route, you might be asked to complete a paper arrival card.
Other conditions
You can be deported if you don't have a valid passport or visa.
You could incur heavy penalties for overstaying your visa, including being jailed.
Some visas require you to register yourself within 14 days of your arrival. If you don't register, you might not be able to depart. Visit the Ministry of Home Affairs website for details.
We can't help you to stay if you don't have the correct documents.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the Indian High Commission in Canberra for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.

Indian authorities have closed the Integrated Check Post (ICP) at the Attari Border (land border between India and Pakistan in the state of Punjab). If you have plans to travel to India from Pakistan using any land borders, make alternate plans and follow the advice of local authorities.
More information:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Border measures

Due to the Ebola disease outbreak overseas, you're now required to complete an online health self-declaration form up to 24 hours before arrival in India. If you don't complete the form before you arrive, expect delays and additional screening procedures at Indian immigration.

If you’re travelling to India from an Ebola affected country, you may be required to undertake a temperature check on arrival. If you show symptoms, you may be subject to self-isolation, quarantine, and/or travel restrictions. Check local media and follow advice of local authorities.
Volunteering
If you're considering volunteer work, contact the nearest Indian embassy or consulate about visa requirements before travelling. This includes students visiting India under the New Colombo Plan.
Volunteer responsibly. Make sure you're contributing in an ethical and meaningful way.
Exit visas

If your passport is lost or stolen, report it to the police and contact the nearest Australian High Commission or Consulate to get a replacement travel document. You'll then need to get an exit visa through the online portal Foreigner's Regional Registration Office (FRRO) before you leave.

Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cards are multiple entry, multi-purpose lifelong visas to visit India. OCI holders are entitled to live and work in India.

India has introduced an electronic OCI (e-OCI) card, which can be used with a valid passport at immigration checkpoints in India. OCI can download their e-OCI card through the OCI Services portal or the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam mobile app.
Existing physical OCI booklets remain valid and will continue to be accepted for travel and other services.

If you receive a new Australian passport and hold an OCI card, you must update your details on the OCI portal. You must do this every time you renew your Australian passport or receive a new Australian passport.
More information:
Overseas Citizen of India Services
e-Arrival Card
You're required to complete the online e-Arrival Card up to 3 days before travel to India. This applies to Australian citizens and Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) card holders.
Depending on your travel route, you might be asked to complete a paper arrival card.
Other conditions
You can be deported if you don't have a valid passport or visa.
You could incur heavy penalties for overstaying your visa, including being jailed.
Some visas require you to register yourself within 14 days of your arrival. If you don't register, you might not be able to depart. Visit the Ministry of Home Affairs website for details.
We can't help you to stay if you don't have the correct documents.
Exit requirements

When you depart India, officials will check where and when you entered the country. If you are exiting on a different passport to the one you entered on, you must apply for a special exit permit before you travel. This includes emergency passports.

If you need to apply for an exit permit, apply on the Foreigner's Regional Registration Office (FRRO). It may take 2 weeks or more for the exit permit to be issued, so factor this into your travel plans when you are booking flights
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the Indian High Commission in Canberra for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.

Indian authorities have closed the Integrated Check Post (ICP) at the Attari Border (land border between India and Pakistan in the state of Punjab). If you have plans to travel to India from Pakistan using any land borders, make alternate plans and follow the advice of local authorities.
More information:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Border measures

Due to the Ebola disease outbreak overseas, you're now required to complete an online health self-declaration form up to 24 hours before arrival in India. If you don't complete the form before you arrive, expect delays and additional screening procedures at Indian immigration.

If you’re travelling to India from an Ebola affected country, you may be required to undertake a temperature check on arrival. If you show symptoms, you may be subject to self-isolation, quarantine, and/or travel restrictions. Check local media and follow advice of local authorities.
Volunteering
If you're considering volunteer work, contact the nearest Indian embassy or consulate about visa requirements before travelling. This includes students visiting India under the New Colombo Plan.
Volunteer responsibly: make sure you're contributing in an ethical and meaningful way.

Tourist visas
If you’re travelling from certain countries, including Australia, you don't need a tourist visa for Fiji. If your stay is less than 4 months, authorities will issue a visa when you arrive.
To get a visa on arrival, you must show proof of booked accommodation and a return ticket.
Before travelling, check Tourism Fiji's frequently asked questions about travelling to Fiji page. If you have a previous criminal record, you may be denied entry into Fiji.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest embassy or consulate of Fiji for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.
Other visas
You may need a visa if you travel for other reasons. Contact the Fiji High Commission for more details.

Visas
Estonia is part of the Schengen Area, meaning you can enter Estonia without a visa in some cases.
In other situations, you'll need to get a visa.
When you first enter the Schengen Area, get an entry stamp from border control staff on your passport.
Always carry your passport, even within the Schengen area.
Entry and exit conditions can change at short notice. Contact the nearest Embassy or Consulate for details about visas, currency, customs and quarantine rules.
Border with Russia

Border crossings between Estonia and Russia can close at short notice. Check with Estonia's 'Go Swift' website before crossing. There may be lengthy delays and private cars bearing Russian number plates are banned from entering Estonia. We continue to advise do not travel to Russia.

You'll need to comply with all Estonian border rules and requirements. Check the Estonia Police and Border Guard Board for more information. Australians with dual Russian or Belarusian nationality may also face lengthy delays or be denied entry.
Be particularly careful in border areas with Russia when travelling in Eastern Estonia. Always be fully aware of where you are, and don't, under any circumstances, approach the border zone.
More information:
Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Government of Estonia
Estonia Police and Border Guard Board

prima: Validity
Many countries require your passport to be valid for at least 6 months before entering or departing. This includes for transit.
If your passport expires too soon, you might not be able to travel.
The Australian Government doesn’t make these rules. Check your passport’s expiry date before you go. If you’re not sure, it’s a good idea to get a new passport.

If you're a non-Australian citizen travelling with an Australian travel document, Bahrain may not issue you an e-visa on arrival as it would for Australian citizens travelling on an Australian passport.

You'll need to contact your nearest Bahraini Embassy/Consulate for up-to-date advice and information on accepting your travel document and to seek options and confirmation on the appropriate visa that will be accepted to enter the country.
If your entry into Bahrain is denied despite you having a valid Bahraini visa, the Australian Embassy in Riyadh won't be able to assist you in facilitating your entry.

Airlines may not allow holders of Australian travel-related documents issued to non-Australian citizens to board flights to Australia. Check your eligibility to re-enter Australia with the Department of Home Affairs and confirm with your airlines before your departure.
Lost or stolen passport
Your passport is valuable and can be used by others to commit crimes.
Don’t let anyone trick you into giving it to them. Always keep it in a safe place.
If your passport is lost or stolen, tell the Australian Government:
In Australia: contact the Australian Passport Information Service.
Overseas: contact the nearest Australian embassy or consulate.
Passport with ‘X’ gender identifier

Australian passports comply with international standards for sex and gender. If your passport has an 'X' in the sex field, we can’t guarantee your entry or transit to other countries. Ask the embassy or consulate of your destinations if they’ll accept your passport with an 'X' gender marker. Check all transit destinations too.
More information:
LGBTQIA+ travellers
